title: Dangerous Goods Acceptance: Number of Acceptances a Customer May Hold
content:
## Clause

A customer of Dangerous Goods Acceptance may hold as many acceptances as it needs; the product sets no maximum per customer. The unit is deliberately small: one acceptance is one UN entry travelling on one booking. How several acceptances may sit side by side is limited only at the level of the booking that carries them and of the sailing they travel on, through the product's booking-mix and sailing-allotment rules.

## The same rule by level

| Level at which acceptances are counted | Ceiling set for this product |
|---|---|
| One customer, across all of its bookings and sailings | none — no per-customer maximum exists |
| One booking | governed by the booking-mix rule |
| One sailing, per customer | governed by the sailing-allotment rule |

## Points of judgement

**A shipper moving three different UN entries on one booking — how many acceptances is that?** Three, one for each UN entry, all on the same booking.

**Can the total number of acceptances a customer already holds, taken on its own, be a ground for refusing another?** No. The customer-level total is not limited; any limit arises only from the booking or the sailing concerned.
